title: SPIRITUAL INTELLIGENCE
mv: The eyes of your understanding being enlightened; that ye may know what is the hope of his calling, and what the riches of the glory of his inheritance in the saints.
mvp: “The eyes of your understanding being enlightened; that ye may know what is the hope of his calling, and what the riches of the glory of his inheritance in the saints.” Ephesians 1:18
assignment: Five (5) characteristics of a spiritually intelligent Christian (2X5=10 marks).

b.x: Spiritual Intelligence is the capacity to perceive, interpret, and respond to life in accordance with God’s wisdom, truth, and purpose. It entails the ability to discern, understand, and apply spiritual truths for effective living and decision-making in accordance with God’s will. It is the wisdom from above that enables a believer to navigate life with a divine view. It involves spiritual discernment, divine wisdom, revelation knowledge and alignment with the Holy Spirit.
Some characteristics of spiritual intelligence include:

i: Discerning - Ability to distinguish between truth and error; good and evil (Hebrews 5:14; 1 John 4:1).
Revelation Knowledge - Insight from the Holy Spirit beyond human reasoning (Ephesians 1:17-18; Colossians 1:9).
Wisdom from God - To practically apply divine knowledge to issues (James 3:17; 1Corinthians 2:6-7).
Fruit of the Spirit - It helps to substantiate spiritual intelligence in character and conduct (Galatians 5:22-23; Ephesians 5:9).
Godly Perspective - Ability to see life through the lens of God’s purpose (Romans 12:2; Ephesians 5:10, 17).

b.x: Joseph displayed spiritual intelligence by interpreting Pharaoh’s dream and giving divine strategy (Genesis 41:39). Daniel operated in knowledge, understanding, and interpretation (Daniel 1:17, 20). Solomon asked for wisdom to lead well, and God gave him great wisdom and understanding (1 Kings 3:9-12; 4:29-30). Paul received the revelation of Christ and wrote deep theological truths (Galatians 1:11-12). Jesus Christ operated with divine wisdom (Luke 2:47; John 5:19).

Spiritual intelligence guides believers in making godly decisions (Proverbs 3:5-6). It builds strong Christian character (2 Peter 1:5-8) and enables spiritual maturity. (1 Corinthians 3:1-3). It also protects against deception (Matthew 24:24).
To grow in spiritual intelligence, believers need to imbibe the culture of:

i: Studying God’s word regularly to be trained in righteousness (2 Timothy 3:16-17).
Praying for wisdom and revelation (James 1:5; Ephesians 1:17).
Walking in the Spirit and not gratifying the flesh (Galatians 5:16).

b.x: Lack of spiritual intelligence can result in spiritual blindness, carnality, poor decision-making and vulnerability. Be spiritually intelligent.

i: State three (3) importance of spiritual intelligence.
Mention two (2) means of becoming spiritually intelligent.
